scenes.title: Bread from the Ravens
beats: Long ago, a king named Ahab and his people stopped loving God. They prayed to a pretend god called Baal instead.
So God’s prophet Elijah told the king, “Because of this, no rain will fall, not one drop, until I say so!”
Then God sent Elijah to hide by a little stream. And every morning and every evening, big black ravens flew down and brought him bread and meat!

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: beside a small, clear stream in a quiet rocky valley with a few trees, in soft golden morning light: Elijah sits on a rock by the water, right of center, smiling up in surprise as two big black ravens swoop down to him, one carrying a round loaf of bread and one carrying a piece of meat in its beak

scenes.title: The Jar That Never Ran Out
beats: After a while the stream dried up. So God sent Elijah to a town where a poor widow lived with her little boy.
“I only have a handful of flour and a little oil left,” she said. “Make me a small loaf first,” said Elijah, “and God won’t let your flour and oil run out.”
And it was true! Every day she reached into her jar, and there was always more flour, and always more oil. God took care of them all.

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: inside a small, simple clay-brick home with a little window and warm light: a kind widow in a faded rose robe pours golden oil from a small jug into a bowl of flour, right of center, while her little boy watches beside her and Elijah sits at the low table smiling; a clay jar of flour glows softly with warm light, full to the top

scenes.title: Who Is the Real God?
beats: Three years later, Elijah called all the people to the top of Mount Carmel, along with 450 prophets of Baal. “Let’s find out who the real God is!” he said.
“We will each build an altar and pray. The God who answers with fire is the real God!” Everyone agreed.
The prophets of Baal shouted and danced around their altar from morning until afternoon. “O Baal, answer us!” But nothing happened. Not a sound. Not one spark.

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: on the wide, rocky top of Mount Carmel under a hazy sky: a big crowd of Baal’s prophets in fancy red and purple robes shout and dance and wave their arms around a stone altar piled with wood, left of center, but nothing happens; Elijah stands calmly right of center with his arms folded and a little smile, and crowds of people watch from the rocks

scenes.title: Fire from Heaven
beats: Then it was Elijah’s turn. He built an altar with twelve stones, put wood on top, and dug a ditch all around it.
“Pour water on it,” Elijah said. “Again! Again!” Splash, splash, splash! The altar was soaking wet, and the ditch was full of water.
Elijah prayed, “Lord, show everyone that You are God!” And WHOOSH! Fire fell from heaven and burned up everything, the wood, the stones, and even the water!
All the people fell to their knees. “The Lord, He is God!” they shouted. And then, at last, the rain came pouring down.

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: on the rocky top of Mount Carmel in the late afternoon: a simple altar of twelve big stones piled with wood, soaked with water and surrounded by a ditch full of water, stands right of center, and Elijah kneels in front of it with his arms raised to heaven in prayer, while a big crowd of people watches quietly from the rocks behind

layers.edit: A great column of bright, glowing fire now falls from the sky onto the altar, burning up the wood and stones in a blaze of golden and orange light, the water in the ditch turning to steam; Elijah kneels with his arms raised, and all the people have fallen to their knees in amazement.

scenes.title: A Chariot of Fire
beats: When Elijah was old, he had a helper and friend named Elisha. They walked together everywhere, and Elisha would not leave his side.
One day, as they were walking and talking, a chariot of fire pulled by horses of fire swept down between them! And Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elijah’s cloak fell to the ground. Elisha picked it up, and God was with Elisha, just as He had been with Elijah.

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: beside the river Jordan in warm golden evening light, with reeds and palm trees along the bank and hills beyond: old Elijah and young Elisha walk side by side along the riverbank, right of center, talking together like good friends

layers.edit: A glowing chariot made of bright fire, pulled by two leaping horses of fire, now sweeps up into the sky in a swirling golden whirlwind, carrying Elijah up toward the clouds; Elijah’s brown cloak floats down toward young Elisha, who stands on the riverbank looking up in wonder.

questions: God sent ravens to bring Elijah food. How does God take care of you?
The prophets of Baal shouted all day and nothing happened. Why do you think Elijah was so sure God would answer?
Elijah prayed, and God answered. What would you like to talk to God about today?

verse.text: The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!
